items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Some of the beautiful Miles Davis, you know the beautiful things, I loved it.

ctx.x: When players in the 60s came along — Coltrane, Miles Davis — the music seemed to get, some of it, pretty angry. Was it something you listened to? Did it have an effect on you?

I just walked away from — I was not that interested. Some of the beautiful Miles Davis, you know the beautiful things, I loved it. The other agendas that go with the playing, the attitudes and things, I try not to let that get in the way of my playing. I think by that time I already had decided kind of where I was going to go musically and didn’t want to get into a lot of that, I thought it would mess my style. Of course I was working in the 60s, I was still working days, I hadn’t made my commitment to go full…

great time. So let’s have a great time together. I don’t believe in goofing off or hacking around, I mean I’ve very, I set pretty high professional standards for myself and the fellows around me, but I mean let’s have a good time and play some darn good music.
